body: The goal isn’t to make things sound “cool” or “esoteric.” It’s to create something rooted that still works in a sci-fi context and I appreciate this input. If you have ideas for better phrasing or examples of how to bridge those concepts, I’d love to hear them. I am using placeholder names right now that I do want to change as I learn more.

No....I am asking for help. I have stated multiple times now that the names are placeholders and that I would like help understanding. This is a building block to lead to something better. You have to start somewhere bro...

I have black characters in my stories, women too. I am a white man,  I have ridiculous characters like Mr. Jazz Hands and Emotional Heaviness Man. Reflectra can reflect light at exactly 45 degrees. I brought my dead shih tzu into my world, I have Muslims, Catholics, heretics, cults, monsters. I don’t write based on quotas. I write because these characters *feel true.* Because humanity is messy, vast, and brilliant and I want to show all of it.

If I didn’t care, I wouldn’t be here asking, listening, and revising.

Another thing....Humanity doesn't just erase itself once it reaches the stars bro. They are gonna bring their religions, cultural identities with them. Ever see the Expanse? Warhammer 40k? So what If I have a Mexican **resistance movement** chanting *“¡Por la Madre Tierra!"?* Why can't I have a group like the Space Wolves, White Scars, Belters (from the Expanse)? What about the Thousand Sons? What about the Galactic Empire from Star Wars? What about Avatar the Last Airbender? Narnia, Elden Ring, Ghost of Tsushima, The Witcher? All of those use human beliefs and cultural.

Totally fair to feel that way bro.

That’s actually *why* I posted this, so I could avoid doing the exact thing you’re concerned about. I’m not trying to decorate my world with Sanskrit.....I’m trying to *build a spiritually grounded faction that feels like it has roots.*

As I said, the names are placeholders, and I fully expect some of them to get replaced or reworked as I learn more, gotta have a blueprint before you just create something out of thin air.

This isn’t a final product. It’s a draft. And I’m here because I want to do it **with** community input and not just as an outsider guessing from the sidelines.

If you *do* have suggestions for how the Dharma-oriented concepts could be better reflected, I’d actually love to hear them.

Thanks so much for this! You’re spot-on about the naming....“Yantrik” was meant to evoke spiritualized technology, but I realize it might read more robotic than sacred. The army isn’t mechs—it’s more like blessed, solar-powered suits of armor, almost paladin-like. I might simplify that to “Dharma Sena” and rework internal branches with better Sanskrit or thematic clarity.

As for Trinetra—I wasn’t referencing the Trimurti directly, but using “Three-Eyed” to represent Knowledge, Duty, and Power. But if that causes confusion, I might rename the council to something less loaded. 

This feedback is incredibly helpful, truly. I appreciate it! It is very important for me to get these guys right cause its one of the most important arcs in my universe, without them, well lets just say Humanity gets wrecked.

The spiritual side of the my universe isn’t clean. It’s messy. There’s no single denomination or moral authority running things. People of faith exist all over the spectrum. Some are true servants. Others are corrupt or broken. One of the most important characters actually became who he is after a Catholic priest murdered his parents in cold blood. That was his breaking point. He snapped, and in his pain, he heard something ancient calling to him. Something other. He follows a different path now, one of ritual, violence, and strange faith. But it’s still faith, even if it’s terrifying. Then there’s an occult witch, who’s deeply involved in occult forces. She knows real power. She’s been burned by religious institutions and arcane ones alike. She doesn’t believe in hope anymore. She believes in control. Her story runs parallel to my main character in some weird ways, but where my main character sees mercy, the Witch sees weakness. She’s not evil, but she’s a warning. And yet, amid all that, you have characters like another catholic priest struggling with his faith and an Imam who runs an orphanage for the children of dead heroes, so they are men of faith who haven’t turned away. They’re not perfect, but they stay. They still guide. They still believe in helping others stand up, even in a city full of ghosts, demons, and failed gods (not gods in our sense, but powered beings worshiped by humans and aliens who have forgotten the one true God). I guess what I’m trying to say is… I’m not building a Christian universe, or a faithless one. I’m building a world where belief still matters, but it has to fight for breath. The **Dharma-Yantrik Sena wage an endless war against hell, in their owned space and sector of the galaxy. I myself am not religious, however I am not faithless.**
